definitions.explanation: A large mass of ice that has broken off from a glacier and floats in the sea. Also used figuratively in the expression 'tip of the iceberg.'

examples.japanese: {氷山|ひょうざん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一角|いっかく}→一角：11231_ikkaku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧すぎない。
examples.english: It is only the tip of the iceberg.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧{氷山|ひょうざん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{海|うみ}→海：00556_umi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{浮|う}かんでいた→浮かぶ：03916_ukabu⟧。
examples.english: A large iceberg was floating in the sea.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{氷山|ひょうざん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一角|いっかく}→一角：11231_ikkaku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{実際|じっさい}→実際：02502_jissai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦もっと→もっと：00798_motto⟧⟦{深刻|しんこく}→深刻：01567_shinkoku⟧な⟦{状況|じょうきょう}→状況：01576_joukyou⟧だ。
examples.english: This problem is just the tip of the iceberg — the actual situation is much more serious.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly encountered in the set phrase {氷山|ひょうざん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一角|いっかく}→一角：11231_ikkaku⟧ (the tip of the iceberg), meaning that what is visible represents only a small portion of a larger problem or situation. This expression parallels the English idiom exactly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {氷山|ひょうざん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一角|いっかく}→一角：11231_ikkaku⟧ (tip of the iceberg)
- {氷山|ひょうざん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{浮|う}かぶ→浮かぶ：03916_ukabu⟧ (an iceberg floats)
- {氷山|ひょうざん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ぶつかる→ぶつかる：02412_butsukaru⟧ (to collide with an iceberg)
